claimChecks.claim: VVF/urethrovaginal/RVF routinely probe-then-director lay open and groove protects all structures
claimChecks.locator: Randazzo operative technique pp 7–10; EAU §§4.8–4.9; ASCRS RVF and anal recommendations pp 2,6–10
claimChecks.note: Localization can use cystoscopy/catheter/wire; anatomy, approach and multilayer repair differ from a routine director-guided incision.

claimChecks.claim: Anal fistulotomy after Goodsall-rule probing is generally safe
claimChecks.locator: Classification Table 1 p2, false tract p6 and simple fistulotomy recommendation p7
claimChecks.note: Selected simple fistula with normal sphincter function may be laid open; inflamed/complex/anterior-in-women and RVF anatomy demand different assessment.

claimChecks.claim: Director and probe are all stainless steel, malleable, autoclavable 00–8, and tip/groove guarantee protection
claimChecks.locator: Aspen 09-1614 specifications; Rev 10 English IFU pp2–5
claimChecks.note: Aspen reusable probe-point director length and reprocessing established for specified model; no universal material, bendability, size range or absolute shielding follows.

claimChecks.claim: Urethral diverticulum is treated by probing neck then director-protected lay-open
claimChecks.note: MRI/cystoscopy and operative excision with watertight multilayer closure are distinct; rare endoscopic incision is not generic director use.

claimChecks.claim: Fine probes are standard for hypospadias, urachal sinus, Skene/Bartholin and radiated sinuses
claimChecks.locator: No representative full operative sources accessed for these niche indications
claimChecks.note: Retained as conditional instrument orientation, not an asserted standard or inevitable incision; procedure-specific sources and local anatomy remain necessary.
